title: Future Of The City Centre Lot
situation: Your city has a small, empty piece of land in the downtown area. The city council is asking residents for their opinion on how to use this space to benefit the community.
options: Build a community garden where residents can grow their own vegetables and flowers.
Build a new parking lot to provide more parking for downtown businesses and shoppers.
samples:
For the empty lot in our city centre, I believe the best choice is Option A, to build a community garden. This would be much more beneficial for our residents than another parking lot.

Firstly, a garden would improve the health and well-being of our community. It gives people a wonderful reason to spend time outside, which is good for both physical and mental health. Also, it would be a social space where neighbours can meet and work together. This helps to build a stronger, more connected community. Families could teach their children how to grow food, which is a valuable life skill.

In addition, a garden is much better for the environment. Creating a green space in the city centre helps to clean the air and makes our downtown look more beautiful. It would be a peaceful, quiet place for people to relax. A parking lot is just more concrete and will only add to the noise and traffic. A community garden would contribute positively to our city for many years. Therefore, I strongly support this option.

I am writing to explain my choice for the new development in the city centre. I believe that Option B, building a new parking lot, is the correct decision for our community at this time.

The most important reason is to support our local economy. Many businesses in the downtown area are struggling because customers cannot find a place to park. If people have to drive around looking for a spot, they often give up and go to a large shopping mall outside the city instead. More parking would bring more shoppers downtown, which is essential for helping our local shops and restaurants succeed. This will keep our city centre active and strong.

Furthermore, a new parking lot would make visiting downtown more convenient for everyone. It would reduce traffic problems caused by cars circling the streets. This would make the area more accessible for older residents and for families with young children who need to park close to their destination. While a garden is a nice idea, solving the parking problem is a more urgent need for our city right now. In conclusion, I strongly recommend we build the parking lot.
